subject: Forecast reconciliation + churn spotlight: BrightByte renewal
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightbyte.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Forecast reconciliation + churn spotlight: BrightByte renewal

Hi team / Alex,

Quick note ahead of Monday's finance sweep — BrightByte (DL-4857) is listed as 95% commit in SFDC but our renewal matrix shows a lower committed ARR once we account for consumption adjustments and the support add-on opt-out. Id like us to reconcile final committed ARR and call out any elevated churn signals so FinOps and Sales Ops can finalize the Q3 close.

Ask list:
- Marissa: please attach the latest customer-level renewal matrix (per-seat vs consumption) and confirm the committed ARR youre putting into the forecast.
- Naomi: run the churn-risk flag for this account (last 90d usage drop, support opt-out, and delayed PO). If you see a >20% risk, flag for escalation.
- Ben: confirm whether finance has received a revised PO / SOW from BrightByte and the expected billing start date.
- Alex / Sara (BrightByte): if the numbers below don't match your expectations, please reply with the consumption estimate you expect to run in the next 12 months. We want to avoid over-committing on the forecast.

Attached: renewal-matrix-v1.xlsx, churn-heatmap-aug2026.png (matrix is per-seat + usage columns).

High-level notes I pulled:
- Sales stage in SFDC: Commit (95%).
- Renewal term: 12 months starting 2026-10-01.
- Current forecasted committed ARR (source: renewal-matrix-v1): $420k.
- Finance invoice cadence: quarterly in advance (Ben to confirm).

Proposed cadence: recon in <48h, update SFDC stage to reflect final committed ARR, and if churn-risk >= 20% open an escalation thread to CS + Leadership.

Thanks — Ill capture the updates in the hub link once I have Marissa's numbers.

--
David Kim
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

> Quick note ahead of Monday's finance sweep — BrightByte (DL-4857) is listed as 95% commit in SFDC but our renewal matrix shows a lower committed ARR once we account for consumption adjustments and the support add-on opt-out.

Thanks, David — attaching the updated matrix (renewal-matrix-v2.xlsx). Summary below:

- Raw contracted ARR (renewal document): $450,000
- Usage adjustment (expected ramp-down next 3 months): -$30,000 ARR
- Support add-on opt-out (customer requested to remove advanced support): -$10,000 ARR
- Final recommended committed ARR for forecast: $410,000 ARR

I updated the SFDC opportunity with the recommended committed amount and left a note under the "Forecast Comments" field pointing to the matrix.

Action items:
- David: if Finance needs a different recognition for Q3 vs Q4, flag here.
- Naomi: please run your churn rubric (I highlighted the signals in tab 'Signals' on the sheet). I circled the usage dip in July and the support opt-out.
- Alex: happy to set a quick 20-min sync if BrightByte wants to walk numbers.

Attachments: renewal-matrix-v2.xlsx

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Director, Renewals
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightbyte.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@brightbyte.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Forecast reconciliation + churn spotlight: BrightByte renewal

Thanks for the transparency and the matrix — appreciate the recon work. A couple quick clarifications from our side before confirming the PO: 

1) Consumption: our Q3 adoption did dip because of an internal pause on the analytics rollout; however we expect consumption to pick back up in Nov once the pipeline integration is complete. The number Marissa used for the 3-month ramp feels conservative to us. I can share expected monthly consumption (projected) — would that be helpful?

2) Support: Sara is cc'd — we are still discussing support tiers internally. If we keep standard support and add a limited escalations bundle, it would land between the full add-on and the opt-out. That could shift ARR +$6k if we take the mid-tier.

3) Billing / PO: we intend to issue a PO by 2026-09-10 but would like the forecast to reflect the optional mid-tier support as a contingent uplift rather than hard commit. Can you indicate how Redwood wants contingent uplifts handled in final forecasts?

Were open to a 20-30 minute call this week to align. Proposed windows: Fri 9/3 10:00-10:30 PDT or Mon 9/6 08:30-09:00 PDT.

Alex
VP, Product Ops
BrightByte
